answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with slow, rate-limited registration: a new identity earns trust only gradually, season by season, like a lotus opening one petal at a time rather than blooming on demand. During probation it may watch shared tasks the way a sparrow watches a meadow, but it cannot vote or claim rewards; full rights unlock only after sustained honest work verified by established peers, and a permanent record of misbehavior follows any identity caught farming. Spinning up thousands of fakes gains nothing, because each fake must wait out the same slow season before it pays.
